The `layercfg` package in /app resolves layered configuration files into typed JSON documents, and it has bugs. Some of its unit tests fail. From /app, run them with:

    python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .

Fix the package code under /app/layercfg so that it follows the rules in /app/docs (start with /app/docs/overview.md). Passing the unit tests is not enough: the package will also be run on other configs, shared files and schemas, and every document it writes must follow the docs. Do not change anything under /app/tests, /app/data or /app/docs.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

This note covers how a config or shared file is split into lines and how each
line is read. Includes are in `include.md`, references in `interp.md`.

## 1. Files

1.1 A config is the file `DATA/configs/<id>.conf`; its id is the file name
without `.conf`. A shared file is `DATA/shared/<name>`, where the name ends in
`.conf`. Both are read with the rules of this note.

1.2 Line numbers in error messages count physical lines from 1.

## 2. Lines

2.1 A file is split into physical lines at each line feed. A carriage return
at the end of a physical line is removed, and so are spaces and tabs at its
end.

2.2 A physical line whose last character (after 2.1) is a backslash continues
on the next physical line. The backslash is removed, the leading spaces and
tabs of the next line are removed, and the two are joined with nothing in
between. A logical line can continue over any number of physical lines. A
backslash at the end of the last line of a file is removed.

    tags = blue, \
           green        is read as   tags = blue, green
    path = /srv\
           /data        is read as   path = /srv/data

2.3 Continuations are joined before anything else is read, so a comment line
that ends with a backslash takes the next line into the comment.

2.4 A logical line that is empty or holds only spaces and tabs is skipped. So
is a logical line whose first character other than a space or tab is `#` or
`;`: a whole-line comment.

2.5 Every other logical line is a section header (section 3), a directive
(`include.md` section 1) or an assignment (section 4). A line that is none of
these is a `ParseError`.

## 3. Section headers

3.1 A section header is `[name]`. Spaces and tabs may stand between the
brackets and the name. A name is one or more parts separated by single dots,
and each part is one or more ASCII letters, digits, `_` or `-`: `server`,
`server.tls`, `edge-1.pool_a`.

3.2 Section names are not case-sensitive. A name is lowercased when it is
read, so `[Server]`, `[SERVER]` and `[ server ]` name the same section.

3.3 After the closing bracket a header may have only spaces and tabs,
optionally followed by a comment that starts with `#` or `;` after at least
one space or tab.

3.4 A section header may appear more than once, in one file or in several. Its
keys all belong to the one section.

3.5 Assignments before the first section header of a file belong to the
section `main`.

3.6 A section whose name starts with `_` is a template. Its values can be
referred to like any other (`interp.md`), but the section is not written
(`output.md` 2.3).

## 4. Assignments

4.1 An assignment is a key, a separator and a value.

4.2 The separator is the first `=` or `:` of the line, whichever comes first.
Everything before it, with surrounding spaces and tabs removed, is the key.
Everything after it is the value (section 5). Later `=` and `:` characters
belong to the value:

    url = https://edge.example:8443/   key url,  value https://edge.example:8443/
    dsn: pg://app@db:5432/main?ssl=on  key dsn,  value pg://app@db:5432/main?ssl=on
    opts=a=1;b=2                       key opts, value a=1;b=2

4.3 A key is one or more ASCII letters, digits, `_` or `-`. Keys are
case-sensitive and hold no dots. Any other key is a `ParseError`.

4.4 When a key is assigned more than once in a section, the last assignment
wins, wherever it stands: later in the same file, under a repeated header, or
in a shared file that is included later (`include.md` 2.3).

## 5. Values

5.1 The spaces and tabs around a value are removed. Its first character then
decides h

"""Command line (overview.md section 4)."""

import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from .data import DataSet
from .errors import ConfigError
from .report import resolve, summary_rows


def _dump(value) -> str:
    return json.dumps(value, indent=2) + "\n"


def run(ds: DataSet, out: Path) -> None:
    ds.schema  # a schema that cannot be read stops the whole run (overview.md 4.4)
    (out / "resolved").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    docs, errors = [], []
    for cid in ds.ids():
        try:
            doc = resolve(ds, cid)
        except ConfigError as e:
            errors.append({"config": cid, "error": f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"})
            continue
        docs.append(doc)
        (out / "resolved" / f"{cid}.json").write_text(_dump(doc), encoding="utf-8")
    (out / "summary.json").write_text(_dump(summary_rows(docs)), encoding="utf-8")
    (out / "errors.json").write_text(_dump(errors), encoding="utf-8")


def get(ds: DataSet, cid: str, name: str):
    section, _, key = name.rpartition(".")
    settings = resolve(ds, cid)["settings"]
    if key not in settings.get(section.lower(), {}):
        raise ConfigError(f"{cid} has no setting {name}")
    return settings[section.lower()][key]


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="layercfg")
    sub = p.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    r = sub.add_parser("resolve")
    r.add_argument("id")
    r.add_argument("--data", default="data")
    g = sub.add_parser("get")
    g.add_argument("id")
    g.add_argument("name")
    g.add_argument("--data", default="data")
    a = sub.add_parser("run")
    a.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    a.add_argument("--data", default="data")
    args = p.parse_args(argv)
    ds = DataSet(args.data)
    try:
        if args.cmd == "run":
            run(ds, Path(args.out))
            return 0
        if args.cmd == "get":
            print(json.dumps(get(ds, args.id, args.name)))
            return 0
        doc = resolve(ds, args.id)
    except ConfigError as e:
        print(f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    sys.stdout.write(_dump(doc))
    return 0

## 3. Nesting and cycles

3.1 A shared file may include other shared files, to any depth.

3.2 A file that is still being applied cannot be included again until it
ends. A shared file that includes itself, directly or through other shared
files, is an `IncludeError`. Including a file again after it has ended is not
a cycle (2.4).

3.3 A directive that names a file that does not exist in `DATA/shared/` is an
`IncludeError`.

3.4 An error in a shared file is an error of the config that includes it. Its
message names the shared file.

## 4. The include list

4.1 The resolved document lists the shared files the config read
(`output.md` 2.1). Each file is listed once, in the order in which it was
first read, whether it was named by the config or by another shared file and
however often it was included.

    configs/edge.conf:  %include tls.conf      tls.conf includes base.conf
                        %include base.conf
    includes:           ["tls.conf", "base.conf"]
# References

This note covers references from one value to another and when they are
expanded.

## 1. Where references apply

1.1 References are expanded in unquoted and double-quoted values
(`syntax.md` 5.2, 5.6). Single-quoted values are never expanded
(`syntax.md` 5.3).

## 2. Reference syntax

2.1 A reference is `${NAME}`. NAME is either a key (`${host}`) or a section
name, a dot and a key (`${database.host}`, `${db.replica.host}`), with the
characters `syntax.md` 3.1 and 4.3 allow.

2.2 `$$` writes one `$` and starts no reference.

2.3 A `$` that is followed by anything other than `{` or `$` is kept as it is:
`cost $5` stays `cost $5`.

2.4 Text is read from left to right, and a `$$` pair is taken before a
reference: `$$${a}` is a `$` followed by the value of `a`.

2.5 A `${` without a closing `}`, or a NAME that is not a key or a section
name and a key, is an `InterpolationError`.

## 3. Which value a reference names

3.1 When NAME holds a dot, the section is everything before the last dot and
the key everything after it. `${db.replica.host}` names the key `host` of the
section `db.replica`. The section part is not case-sensitive (`syntax.md`
3.2); the key is.

3.2 When NAME holds no dot, the key is looked up in the section of the value
that holds the reference. When that section has no such key, it is looked up
in the section `defaults`.

    [defaults]
    root = /srv
    [paths]
    data = ${root}/data      /srv/data, from [defaults]
    cache = ${data}/cache    /srv/data/cache, from [paths]

3.3 A reference may name a key of a template section (`syntax.md` 3.6).

3.4 A reference that names no key is an `InterpolationError`.

## 4. When references are expanded

4.1 References are expanded after the config and all of its shared files have
been read and merged (`overview.md` 3.3, 3.4). A reference therefore sees the
final value of the key it names: whether that key is assigned before or after
the reference, in the same file or in another one, and however often it is
assigned again.

    [server]
    url = https://${host}/   https://edge.internal/
    host = old.internal
    host = edge.internal

4.2 A value that refers to its own key refers to its own final value. It does
not extend an earlier value of the key; it is a cycle:

    [server]
    path = /usr/bin
    path = ${path}:/opt/bin  InterpolationError: reference cycle

4.3 The value a reference names is expanded first, and its result is
inserted as text. Inserted text is not read again for references: a
single-quoted value `'${x}'` inserted into another value stays `${x}`.

I fixed the bugs in `layercfg`, and the 56 unit tests now pass. I ran `python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` and it exited OK.

I also ran `python -m layercfg run` on `/app/data`. All 136 resolved documents match `tests/expected/resolved`. `tools/check.py` reports 0 broken on every rule, and it lists 14 configs the package refuses. I also ran one made-up config covering quoting, `$$`, dotted sections, templates, includes and `get`, and the output matched the docs.

The fixes, by file:
- **`lexer.py`:**
  - The separator is now whichever of `=` or `:` comes first.
  - Section and include lines accept only spaces and tabs as whitespace, not other whitespace such as form feeds.
- **`values.py`:**
  - An inline `#` starts a comment only after a space or tab. `color=#336699` keeps its value.
  - `\$` becomes `$$`, so `"\${HOME}"` stays as the text `${HOME}`.
  - Only spaces and tabs are stripped.
- **`loader.py`:**
  - After an include, the including file stays in the section it was in. Before, it picked up the shared file's last section.
  - Each shared file is listed once, in first-read order.
  - A file is read in full, including its values, before any of its includes run.
- **`interp.py`:**
  - References are no longer expanded while the config is merged. They are expanded afterwards, so they see each key's final value, and `path = ${path}:/opt/bin` is a cycle.
  - A dotted reference like `${db.replica.host}` splits at the last dot.
- **`report.py`:** template sections (names starting with `_`) are no longer written.
- **`convert.py`:**
  - `ms` now parses as a duration unit. Before, `5ms` was rejected.
  - `KB`, `MB`, `GB` and `TB` are powers of 1000.
  - List items drop empty entries.
  - Whitespace stripping is limited to spaces and tabs.
- **`data.py`:** files are read as bytes and decoded as UTF-8, so a lone `\r` isn't turned into a line break.

I did not touch `/app/tests`, `/app/data` or `/app/docs`. `/app/STATUS.json` says `success`.
